claimed_purpose.text: LangChain SDK for agent long-term memory on LangGraph's Store: LLM-driven extraction/consolidation, semantic/episodic/procedural patterns, hot-path tools plus background managers, optional prompt optimization—not a hosted companion product.

mechanisms.text: Store: MemoryItem documents in a namespaced BaseStore (Postgres/in-memory); curated {kind, content} writes via create_memory_store_manager or agent manage/search tools—not a raw chat log.

Write: extraction passes existing memories so the model can insert, update, or delete (RemoveDoc → adelete); background_quickstart + ReflectionExecutor defer consolidation; episodic guide stores vector-indexed episodes after turns.
Retrieve: semantic search (query_limit), optional episodic block in system prompt, procedural text in prompt; hot-path quickstart uses agent-decided tool calls unless you add scaffolding.
Isolation: namespace tuples (e.g. langgraph_user_id); checkpointer thread_id for session state vs cross-thread store; InMemoryStore is non-durable across restarts.
Ops: Postgres/integration issues (#42, #154, #114) and tool strict-mode bugs remain field risks; graph_rag prototype removed from seed open_code (demo only).

ledger.claim: The store (long-term, cross-thread) is architecturally distinct from the checkpointer (short-term, per-thread conversation history).
ledger.quote: The store lets you store any information according to preferred hierarchy. The checkpointer tracks state (including the conversation history) within each "thread" for durable execution. They can address overlapping concerns, but the store is more flexible and well-suited for long-term, cross-thread memory.

ledger.claim: LangMem's summarization truncation can silently drop ToolMessages that correspond to parallel tool calls in an AIMessage, breaking downstream graph execution
ledger.quote: LangMem's memory-summarizer, however, may truncate the conversation inside _preprocess_memory_messages. During this truncation it can silently drop some (or all) of the required ToolMessages after the AIMessage. The current code does not detect or correct such a partial removal, so the downstream graph receives an AIMessage with an incomplete set of ToolMessages and the run fails.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: The fix attempt adds post-hoc appending of matching ToolMessages when the summarization boundary falls on an AIMessage with tool calls, but the issue reports this does not cover all parallel-tool-call failure cases
ledger.label: inferred

contested.text: Docs and blog claim consistency via passing existing memories into extractors; issues #42 and #154 report Postgres memories not updating/deleting and unclear persistence—treat production store behavior as contested until verified on your backend.
README says agents 'know when to search'; conceptual guide lists retrieval modes but not a fixed always-on policy—continuity depends on tool binding and host graph design.

Marketing frames semantic + episodic + procedural 'lifelong learning'; issue #41 asks whether types can be combined/adaptively selected—productized typing vs integrator-defined schemas is unresolved in issues.

copy.text: Pattern worth studying: namespaced store + agent-controlled manage/search tools + LLM consolidation pass over prior memories (closer to Mem0/Letta than companion chat logs).

refuse.text: Refuse assuming LangGraph Platform default store equals companion-grade memory without configuring namespace, reflection, and delete/update paths for your user model.
Refuse third-party comparison or benchmark posts (Graphlit, Mem0 benchmark roundups, agent marketcap/niteagent) as behavior specs; use github.io docs, launch blog, and pinned code.
Refuse src/langmem/graph_rag.py demo ingest as production architecture; it was dropped from open_code as commented prototype only.

unknowns.text: Retrieve policy: it is unclear whether memory search is always triggered or adaptive (agent-decided). The README says the agent 'knows when to search' but does not specify the policy or mechanism.
Isolation scope: namespace parameter is shown but the README does not state whether namespaces map to users, sessions, agents, or characters.
No documentation on how vector indexing or embedding is configured within the extraction module itself; indexing behaviour is delegated to the BaseStore implementation and not described here.
Forget / explicit delete API: the page states memories can be deleted/invalidated but does not document a delete call or forget interface in the core API section.
The page does not describe the retrieval policy — when stored memories are selected back into the prompt and under what conditions the system stays silent.
Conflict / supersession: no description of what happens when a newly extracted episode contradicts or duplicates an existing one.

Forget / delete behavior: the manage_memory tool is stated to support delete, but no detail on how deletion is triggered, what the delete API looks like, or whether deleted memories are hard-removed or soft-hidden from retrieval.
Retrieve policy: no description of when or whether retrieval is adaptive (always retrieve vs. only when relevant); the example always calls store.search() on every turn.

No explicit API for hard-delete vs soft-hide at retrieve time: the page describes enable_deletes as removing memories but does not clarify whether deletion is a store-level purge or a retrieval filter.
Versioned history is mentioned but no API for reading, rolling back, or expiring past versions is described on this page.
The page does not describe how or whether the summary produced by _preprocess_memory_messages is persisted across sessions or only used within the current turn's context window

Whether the issue is a bug in LangMem's tool wiring (store not passed through to tool internals) or a misconfiguration — the page reports the symptom but no resolution or maintainer response is visible in the extracted text
It is unclear from this page whether LangMem exposes lower-level hooks (persist, retrieve, forget, conflict resolution) that would allow full custom store substitution.
The page does not address any core memory behaviors (persist, retrieve, forget, conflict). It is a feature-request issue asking about TypeScript support, containing no memory-mechanism claims.
The page does not explain why the extraction graph fails to hit a stop condition even with max_steps=1 set, leaving the interaction between max_steps and LangGraph's recursion_limit undefined.
No documentation on how ReflectionExecutor resolves the named graph internally or what configuration is required for cross-graph dispatch to succeed
No description of how memories are persisted to or retrieved from the store on this page; canonical tool API page that should describe persist/retrieve/forget behavior does not.
Whether LangMem supports combining semantic and episodic memory types, and whether the model can adaptively select which memory type to retrieve at runtime, is not answered on this page.
The page does not show whether the failure is in the write path (extract/supersession logic), the PostgresStore adapter, or the model's tool-calling; the root cause and any resolution are absent
Whether LangMem memory storage can be used directly in LCEL chain flows outside of create_react_agent is asked but not answered on this page.
No description of forget/delete behavior or conflict/supersession logic on this page.
